text:
alex: Heads up — prod dashboards LCP jumped ~1.2s after last night's canary. Charts are slow to first paint on cold load. Seeing increased main bundle size in S3.

maya: ugh, we saw that in telemetry too. dashboard.main LCP p50 up from 900ms -> 2.1s for EU users. :grimacing:

jamie: any obvious culprit from sourcemaps or artifact diffs?

sahil: quick grep of the build artifacts shows a new dependency pulled by metrics-client: 
```
+ node_modules/@redwood/telemetry-metrics/dist/index.js
```
It seems to bundle an Intl polyfill and lodash chunk inlined. main.js increased by ~1.1MB.

alex: that's the package added as part of the rollout to increase telemetry detail. Can we confirm footprint?

maya: ran a size breakdown on canary artifact: 
```
main.js: 2.9MB (was 1.8MB)
vendors~intl: 700KB (new)
lodash.*: 320KB (new duplication)
```
Also noticed client boot path now imports `formatters.js` eagerly.

jamie: if formatters imports Intl polyfill synchronously that explains LCP hit. We should lazy-load formatters where only charts that need advanced formatting request it.

alex: agree. two options: rollback the canary immediately or hot-fix to dynamic import + temporary webpack alias to use smaller intl locale subset. Which is quicker?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout at 2026-03-20T23:40:12Z -> 10% hosts.

sahil: rollback is fastest to restore perf. Hotfix will need a new build and deploy which may take 20-30m + post-deploy validation.

maya: rollback then iterate; also add a build-time check to fail PRs that increase main bundle >200KB. We don't have that gate right now.

jamie: I'll open a quick PR to revert the telemetry-metrics dependency bump and add a TODO to re-land with dynamic import.

alex: thanks. @jamie mind triggering rollback once PR is merged? @deploy-bot can we get a rollback playbook link?

deploy-bot: Rollback playbook: https://internal.company/rollbacks/console-canary. Run `./scripts/rollback_canary.sh --percent 0` from ci-runner.

jamie: PR opened: https://scm/redwood/console/pulls/1489 — reverting metrics-client change and adding webpack-sizes CI check.

maya: once rollback is live let's validate LCP and spot-check charts in EU. I'll run synthetic job.

alex: timeline: rollback now, confirm EU LCP returns to baseline within 15m, then rework telemetry to lazy-load. Assigning: jamie rollback+PR, maya validate, sahil follow-up on telemetry packaging.

sahil: noted. Also will add an eslint/webpack rule to block adding polyfills to main bundle without an explicit flag.

jamie: rolling back now. running `./scripts/rollback_canary.sh --percent 0` (CI run id 84321).

deploy-bot: CI run 84321 started; approx 7 min ETA.

maya: pre-rollback p50 LCP EU snapshot: 2.05s. will post post-rollback.

deploy-bot: CI run 84321 completed; canary percent set to 0 at 2026-03-21T00:02:18Z.

maya: post-rollback p50 LCP EU snapshot: 0.92s. charts look normal in the sampled sessions. :tada:

alex: nice. keeping this thread for the follow-up telemetry packaging work. reminders: avoid synchronous intl, vendor dedupe, and add bundle-size gate.

jamie: will follow up with a design doc for lazy telemetry + smaller locales list.

sahil: thanks everyone. I'll draft the webpack rule and eslint rule and land in a separate PR.
